title: Princeton University Press Partners with Cashmere on AI Licensing
excerpt: Princeton University Press partnered with Cashmere, an AI content-licensing platform, to make its academic catalog available to 'copyright-compliant' AI tools focused on retrieval-augmented generation. A concrete shift toward publishers building sanctioned, no-training licensing pipelines they control rather than only fighting scraping.

title: More Typos, Fewer Em Dashes: Writers Are Creating an Anti-AI 'Literary Counterculture'
excerpt: Novelists, journalists and essayists deliberately introduce typos, sentence fragments and fewer em-dashes to avoid sounding like a chatbot, forming an anti-AI 'literary counterculture'; some literary magazines now add 'no AI polish' notes to submission guidelines. A craft-level shift in how prose signals human authorship.
